10883: OAuth 2.0 Scope
10884: 1
10885: freshdesk.contacts.search
10886: Use custom contact fields that you have created in your account to filter through the contacts and get a list of contacts matching the specified contact fields.
10887: Format - "(contact_field:integer OR contact_field:'string') AND contact_field:boolean"
10888: Note:
10889: 1. Deleted contacts will not be included in the results
10890: 2. The query must be URL encoded
10891: 3. Query can be framed using the name of the contact fields, which can be obtained from Contact Fields endpoint. Contact Fields are case sensitive
10892: 4. Query string must be enclosed between a pair of double quotes and can have up to 512 characters
10893: 5. Logical operators AND, OR along with parentheses () can be used to group conditions
10894: 6. Relational operators greater than or equal to :> and less than or equal to :< can be used along with date fields and numeric fields
10895: 7. Input for date fields should be in UTC Format
10896: 8. The number of objects returned per page is 30 also the total count of the results will be returned along with the result
10897: 9. To scroll through the pages add page parameter to the url. The page number starts with 1 and should not exceed 10
10898: 10. To filter for fields with no values assigned, use the null keyword
10899: 11. Please note that the updates will take a few minutes to get indexed, after which it will be available through API

11597: In order to export contacts using the Freshdesk API, you'll need to make two different API calls.
11598: Step 1: You'll first need to hit the following endpoint with details about your export. This will start the background job and get you a contact export ID.
11599: post

11638: Step 2: The contact export ID can be passed to another endpoint which will return a URL to the exported CSV file.
11639: get

11641: OAuth 2.0 Scope

11644: This endpoint will return a valid URL to the CSV only when the export is done completely. The background job can take anywhere between a few seconds to several minutes to complete depending on the no of contacts and the no of fields you're including in your export. We recommend that you come up with a pre-defined interval and make the API call more than once in order to get the URL in the response.
11645: Note: Every Freshdesk account will be restricted to running only one contact export at a time. Once the export is complete, the exported file can be accessed using the URL for 15 days, post which it will get removed automatically.

11846: Set to true if the field is mandatory in the customer portal. The default Value is false

11848: Set to true if the customers can see the field in the customer portal. The default Value is false
11849: required_for_agents
11850: Set to true if the field is mandatory for agents. The default Value is false

11852: Set to false if the agent cannot edit the fields in the agent interface. The default Value is true

12998: To create a new contact field, use the following APIs.

13000: Attributes
13001: Type
13002: Description
13003: label *
13004: string
13005: Display name for the field (as seen by agents)
13006: label_for_customers *
13007: string
13008: Display name for the field (as seen in the customer portal)
13009: type *
13010: string
13011: For custom contact fields, type of value associated with the field will be given (Examples custom_date, custom_text...)
13012: editable_in_signup
13013: boolean
13014: Set to true if the field can be updated by customers during signup. The default Value is false
13015: position
13016: integer
13017: Position of the company field. If not given, the position value will be 1. The maximum position value that can be given is the number of fields available plus 1.
13018: required_for_agents
13019: boolean
13020: Set to true if the field is mandatory for agents. The default Value is false
13021: agents_can_edit **
13022: boolean
13023: Set to false if the agent cannot edit the fields in the agent interface. The default Value is true
13024: displayed_for_agents **
13025: boolean
13026: Set to false if the agent cannot view the fields in the agent interface. The default Value is true
13027: quick_add_for_agent **

14146: Service Accounts
14147: A service account is a non-human agent that integrations use to call the Freshdesk API with its own API key. It does not use a paid agent seat and cannot sign in to the web or mobile apps. Service accounts are never assigned tickets and are excluded from ticket routing, even when added to groups. Access is controlled through roles, ticket scope and groups. Each service account can hold a primary key and, during a key rotation, a secondary key, so you can rotate keys without downtime.

16031: You can organise your agents into different groups so they could focus on one kind of problem, and get to know the solutions and customers better.

16069: Every group uses certain fixed numerical values to denote the type of its automatic ticket assignment configuration. It is represented by the key auto_ticket_assign. These numerical values along with their meanings are given below.

16073: 0
16074: Round Robin
16075: 1
16076: Skill Based Round Robin
16077: 2
16078: Load Based Round Robin*

19694: Custom Objects
19695: Freshdesk offers objects that are native to a helpdesk system, like tickets, contacts, and companies. These objects form the core of any business and contain the basic information related to the issue (ticket) a particular customer (contact) mapped to an organization (company) is facing. This basic information might fall short in helping agents get the full context behind the ticket. And at scale, it becomes necessary to provide contextual support proactively.
19696: With 'Custom Objects', powered by Freshworks Neo, you can create and bring in information specific to your business use-cases right within Freshdesk and enable your agents to offer a contextual and faster resolution. With 'Custom Objects' enabled in your account, you can create your custom data entities and thus extend the data model in Freshdesk to solve your business use-cases. More information about Custom Objects can be found here
19697: Note: Custom Objects can be enabled on request for accounts on Enterprise plan.
19698: Custom Object Attributes

19800: You can create a Custom Object through the UI by providing its Name, Description and Icon. You can also add the fields and lookup relationships between the Objects (both Custom and Native) through the UI. More information can be found here

20379: Filter Records Of A Custom Object
20380: get
20381: /api/v2/custom_objects/schemas/{schema_id}/records?{field-name}{operator}{value}
20382: OAuth 2.0 Scope
20383: 1
20384: freshdesk.custom_objects.records.view
20385: The query parameters can be specified to filter the records. The query parameters is a list of conditions connected by the AND operator. A condition consists of three components i.e Operand, Operator and Value. For Custom Object records, Operand is the Field name and Value is the Field Value. Example: {field_name}{operator}{field_value}
20386: Supported Operators
20387: Operator
20388: URL Encoded Equivalent
20389: Description
20390: =
20391: =
20392: Equal to
20393: >
20394: %5Bgt%5D=
20395: Greater than
20396: <
20397: %5Blt%5D=
20398: Less than
20399: >=
20400: %5Bgte%5D=
20401: Greater than or equal to
20402: <=
20403: %5Blte%5D=
20404: Less than or equal to
20405: Note:
20406: 1. System fields 'created_time' and 'updated_time' can also be used as the Operands. These fields must be provided in YYYY-MM-DDTHH:mm:ss.SSSZ format.
20407: 2. The Operator and the Field value must be URL encoded (See sample code below)
20408: 3. The Operators != (Not equal to) and 'OR' are not supported
20409: 4. To filter records using a Lookup field, the ID of the Object should be specified as the field value.
20410: - For Tickets, display_id should be used as the field value
20411: - For Contacts, org_contact_id should be used as the field value.
20412: - For Companies, org_company_id should be used as the field value
20413: - For Custom Objects, id of the record should be used as the Lookup field value

20420: Sort the records by the Field name
20421: sort_order

20423: Order of sorting the records (ASC or DESC)
20424: Note:
20425: 1. Sorting can only be performed on the filterable fields. By default, the result is sorted on the Created Time
20426: 2. Although sorting can be performed on the dropdown fields, the order of data will be in an arbitrary fashion.

20851: Canned Responses
20852: Canned Responses are predefined reply templates which can be used to quickly send out replies to tickets. Canned Responses reside
20853: inside canned response folders. These APIs allow access to the folders and responses under the folders.
20854: Note:
20855: Only users with admin privileges can access the following APIs.

20857: Type
20858: Description

20862: name
20863: string
20864: Name of the canned response folder
20865: personal
20866: boolean
20867: Set true if the folder can be accessed only by you
20868: responses_count
20869: number

20871: created_at
20872: datetime
20873: Canned Response Folders creation timestamp
20874: updated_at
20875: datetime

Furthermore, if a critical issue or idea is raised in the community, you can convert it into a ticket and get your team to work on it right away.

22928: Solutions
22929: An effective knowledge base solves two of the biggest help desk problems. First, since all agents have a common place to pool in and share solutions, you can be sure that customer responses are consistent throughout. Second, since customers can access and help themselves to solutions, they feel more confident about your business. And all the while, your support load reduces.
22930: For better clarity, the Freshdesk knowledge base is categorized into a three level hierarchy - top level Categories that hold related Folders and Solution Articles inside each folder.
22931: Categories
22932: Categories broadly classify your solutions page into several sections. For example, you could place Shipping, Payments and Delivery related information under the Order Fulfilment category. Another interesting application of the top level category is when you are providing support across multiple brands or products.

25674: Customer SatisfactionNEW
25675: Freshdesk offers two sets of Customer Satisfaction (CSAT) APIs. Use the guide below to determine which APIs are applicable to your account.
25676: API Compatibility
25677: New CSAT APIs: Applicable for accounts which signed up from December 2025 onwards or have upgraded to the New CSAT.
25678: Legacy CSAT APIs: Applicable for existing customers which signed up before December 2025 and haven't upgraded to the New CSAT. Learn More.
25679: Upgraded to the New CSAT from the Legacy CSAT?
25680: If you upgraded from the Legacy CSAT to the New CSAT via the mandated Freshdesk Omni 2025 upgrade flow or the self-service opt-in flow, your existing Legacy API implementations will continue to work through backward compatibility. However, we strongly recommend switching to the new CSAT APIs.
25681: Why: Once you modify the existing survey configuration or add new surveys, legacy compatibility ends. You must switch to the New CSAT APIs at that time to ensure functionality.
25682: Use the below endpoints to retrieve complex survey structures including range, text, and choice questions, as well as submitting multi-part responses.

25877: Type
25878: Description

25900: Type
25901: Description

25907: button_stylestringOne of: highlighted, standard.

26303: Satisfaction Ratings
26304: Every response to a customer satisfaction survey is recorded as a satisfaction rating. These ratings are used to generate a customer satisfaction report that you can use to see which of your agents have received the most number of happy ratings, and who hasn't been very helpful to your customers. 26514: Overview
26515: Freshdesk’s Field Service Management (FSM) allows your support agents and field technicians to work together to deliver stellar support to your customers. With the FSM module enabled in your account, you can onboard and dispatch field technicians, plan their schedules, pass on information of the customer to them for context, and live-track progress as they solve problems on-site.
26516: With the help of these REST APIs listed here, you can perform read, modify, add and delete operations on Service Tasks, Service Groups and Field Technicians.
26517: To view the list of apps available for Field Service Management, visit our
26518: app marketplace.
26519: Before You Dive In
26520: To enable Field Service Management in Freshdesk:
26521: Login to your account as an Administrator.
26522: Go to Admin > Field Service Management under General Settings.
26523: Click on Enable to enable Field Service Management for your account.
26524: You will be redirected to the landing page for FSM; from here, you can add field technicians,
26525: create service groups and access reports. For more information, view these articles.
26526: Service Task
26527: A service task is a ticket assigned to a field technician. It outlines an upcoming job and describes the work to be done along with information that the field technician would need like location, site contact details, and appointment date and time.
26528: Create a Service Task

26531: OAuth 2.0 Scope

26535: Note:
26536: It is mandatory that the value of ‘Type’ parameter is ‘Service Task’.
26537: A maximum of 10 service tasks can be created for a parent ticket.
26538: This API request could have the parent_id parameter. Parent_id is the ID of the parent ticket to which the service task is attached. For more information on Parent Child Ticketing refer to this section.
26539: In addition to the parameters available for Create A Ticket API, the following parameters are available:

27202: Time Entries
27203: The time tracking feature in Freshdesk lets you track the time spent by each agent on resolving tickets and thereby enables you to gain visibility on the helpdesk's overall performance. Freshdesk lets agents track the time they spend on a ticket with automatic start and stop timers. Agents can also manually log the time they have spent, and detail their activities during this period by adding comments to the time entries.

29864: Omnichannel Activities
29865: The activity API allows you and your agents to record activities from an external application or system in Freshdesk's contact timeline. Pushing information from your applications about a user can provide rich contextual information to your support agents using Freshdesk. Activities published using this API would show up on the contact timeline giving your agents a complete view of the customer’s journey.
29866: Publish Activities
29867: post
29868: /api/v2/contact-activities
29869: OAuth 2.0 Scope
29870: 1
29871: freshdesk.contact_activities.create
29872: Parameters
29873: Attribute
29874: Type
29875: Description
29876: activityMandatory
29877: object
29878: Key value pair of the object which describes information about action that has occurred in an external application.
29879: ATTRIBUTE
29880: TYPE
29881: DESCRIPTION
29882: name Mandatory
29883: string
29884: The name of the activity performed (this is the text which is visible in the contact timeline).
29885: timestamp
29886: string
29887: The time at which the activity was performed. If not given, this would be populated with the time at which we received activity.
29888: description
29889: string
29890: User friendly description of the activity
29891: link
29892: string
29893: Link to the activity
29894: actorMandatory
29895: object
29896: Key value pair of the object which describes the person or entity performed the activity.
29897: sourceMandatory
29898: object
29899: Key value pair of the object which describes the application, where the activity was performed.
29900: object
29901: object
29902: Key value pair of the object which describes the object on which activity was performed.
29903: context
29904: object
29905: Key value pair of the object which can be used to send additional context about the activity. It should adhere to the JSON schema https://json-schema.org
29906: contactMandatory
29907: object
29908: Key value pair of the object which represent Freshdesk contact information for identifying which contact to send the activity against. If the contact doesn’t exist with the given property, it will create a new contact.
29909: ATTRIBUTE
29910: TYPE
29911: DESCRIPTION
29912: email *
29913: string
29914: Email address of the contact
29915: twitter_id *
29916: string
29917: Twitter handle of the contact
29918: unique_external_id *
29919: string
29920: External ID of the contact
29921: facebook_id *
29922: string
29923: Facebook ID of the contact
29924: id *
29925: number
29926: ID of the contact
29927: name
29928: string
29929: Name of the contact
29930: is_actor
29931: boolean
29932: Used to define whether the actor who performed the activity is the contact or not. Default value is true, i.e we assume that the contact has performed the activity.
29933: *One of these five attributes is mandatory
29934: The following table lists the attributes of actor:
29935: Attribute
29936: Type
29937: Description
29938: id
29939: string
29940: ID of the actor.
29941: typeMandatory
29942: string
29943: The type of the actor. As an example, the type could be "agent", "shopper", "user", "customer", "system".
29944: name
29945: string
29946: Name of the actor.
29947: The following table lists the attributes of source:
29948: Attribute
29949: Type
29950: Description
29951: id
29952: string
29953: ID of the application, where the activity was performed.
29954: nameMandatory
29955: string
29956: Name of the application where the activity was performed.
29957: The following table lists the attributes of object:
29958: Attribute
29959: Type
29960: Description
29961: type
29962: string
29963: Type of the object. As an example, the type could be "call", "transaction", "cart", "website".
29964: id

34: OAuth implementation in apps
35: Apps use the Freshdesk REST APIs to access Freshdesk data (resources). API authentication is a process that verifies the identity of app users who want to access the Freshdesk data. API authentication ensures that only authorized users have access to the data.
36: We offer the following API authentication mechanisms to access Freshdesk resources:
37: Basic access authentication. For information on this, see API Authentication using API keys.
38: OAuth authorization and access token authentication. This section explains how your apps can use OAuth authorization.
39: Through OAuth authorization, the apps access the resources securely, without collecting or exposing sensitive credentials from the app user. Freshworks enables you to implement OAuth authorization flows in Freshworks apps and Custom apps.
40: Important:OAuth implementation is supported on all categories of apps: front-end, serverless, and SMI apps.
41: Notes:
42: Freshworks apps are built using the FDK and published to the Freshworks Marketplace. Custom apps are built using the FDK and are private to an organization.
43: In this document, any app (Freshworks or Custom) that uses OAuth flow is called an OAuth app.
44: The OAuth authorization and authentication flow, on successful implementation,
45: Enables app users to authorize the app to act on their behalf to access Freshdesk data.
46: Enables the app to request user's authorization and place a request for an access token.
47: Enables the app to obtain the access token and place authenticated REST API calls.

67: Understanding Freshdesk Pricing Plans

69: TABLE OF CONTENTS
70: About our products and plans
71: Subscription plans
72: Activate a plan

80: Freshdesk offers flexible pricing plans designed to scale with your business as it grows. Whether you’re starting with a single support channel or managing multichannel operations, our plans provide the flexibility to choose what fits your team’s size, budget, and complexity.
81: Prerequisites:
82: Ensure that you have account admin permissions to access the Plans & Billing page.
83: About our products and plans
84: We offer two core products that differ by capabilities and channel support:
85: Freshdesk Omni (Most Popular)
86: Freshdesk Omni is our multichannel support platform that allows you to manage customer interactions from email, chat, social media, and more, all from a unified inbox.
87: Freshdesk (Email-first)
88: Freshdesk is ideal for teams that primarily manage support through email. It provides the foundational ticketing, collaboration, and automation tools required to deliver efficient customer service.
89: Subscription plans
90: Both Freshdesk Omni and Freshdesk offer three flexible plans - Growth, Pro, and Enterprise. Each plan builds on the previous one, adding more customization, automation, and AI-powered features.
91: PlanIdeal forHighlights
92: Freshdesk Omni
93: Growth
94: Small and medium businesses
95: Includes knowledge base, automation, and basic reporting.
96: Pro
97: Scaling businesses
98: Adds advanced ticket routing, analytics dashboards, and WhatsApp campaigns.
99: Enterprise
100: Large organizations
101: Offers advanced customization, strong data security, audit logs, and AI capabilities.
102: Freshdesk
103: Growth
104: Small teams
105: Enables reporting, automation, and a self-service knowledge base.
106: Pro
107: Expanding teams
108: Adds advanced routing, custom roles, and stronger analytics.
109: Enterprise
110: Large teams
111: Adds advanced configuration, multiple SLAs, and enterprise-grade controls.
112: You can view the complete list of features in your Plans and Billing page or our Pricing Page.
113: Activate a plan
114: When you sign up for Freshdesk or Freshdesk Omni, you start with a 14-day trial that provides full access to all product features. After the trial, you can continue using the product by enrolling in the Free Program or by purchasing a paid plan.
115: Trial period
116: Every new account starts with a 14-day free trial that includes:
117: Full feature access: You can try automation, AI capabilities, analytics, and multichannel support.
118: Plan comparison: Switch between Growth, Pro, and Enterprise to determine which plan suits your business best.
119: Unlimited testing: Add agents, configure workflows, and explore integrations without restrictions.
120: During the trial period, you can track plan differences from either the Plans & Billing page within your account or the Pricing Page.
121: At the end of the trial, you can purchase any paid plan to continue seamlessly or move to the Free Program if you’re still evaluating.
122: Tip: If you wish to extend your trial period, please conatct your account manager or send an email to sales@freshdesk.com. For quick assistance, please include your account details (URL, company name) in the email.
123: Free program (Freshdesk only)
124: If you are a Freshdesk customer, you can switch to the Freshdesk Free Program and continue using the product at no cost for 6 months with a limited agent seat (two). The Free Program is specifically designed for small businesses and startups that want to manage customer communication while evaluating advanced features.
125: Note: The Free program applies only to Freshdesk customers and not available in Freshdesk Omni. Also, when you switch from a higher plan during the trial period to the Free Program, certain features and their configurations will be lost. For more information, see Explore Freshdesk Free Program.
126: To join the Free Program:
127: Log in to your Freshdesk account as an Account Admin and click Admin > Plans and Billing.
128: Click Switch plan.
129: Click Try out our Free Program.
130: Paid plans
131: Once you are ready to unlock advanced capabilities and scale your operations, you can choose a paid subscription. Each subscription plan is charged on a per-agent basis, and the total cost is determined by the number of agents in your account.
132: Note: Unless stated, the subscription charges do not include any taxes, levies, duties or similar governmental assessments, including value-added, sales, use or withholding taxes assessable by any local, state, provincial or foreign jurisdiction (collectively 'Taxes').
133: To purchase a paid plan:
134: Log in as an Account Admin and click Admin > Plans and Billing.
135: Click Switch plan.
136: Select the product (Freshdesk or Freshdesk Omni).
137: Select your preferred plan and click Proceed to payment.
138: Enter the number of agents.
139: Select the billing cycle. The options are monthly, annual, quarterly, or half-yearly subscriptions.
140: Select the currency.
141: Note: Only trial customers can change their currencies. After upgrading to a paid plan, your currency setting becomes fixed and cannot be modified via the Plan & Billing page. To request a change, contact billing@freshworks.com.
142: Click Add card and pay.
143: You can pay via credit cards, bank transfer, or PayPal (paypal@freshdesk.com). To use PayPal, ensure that you have a PayPal business ID.
144: Enter your billing information, card details, and click Subscribe.
145: Once payment is completed successfully, your plan becomes active right away. You can see your invoice on the Plans and Billing page, and a copy will be emailed to your registered email address. You may update your payment details anytime or contact us at billing@freshworks.com.
146: Manage subscriptions
147: Once you have purchased a plan and have an active subscription, you can view and manage all aspects of your product subscription directly from the Plans & Billing page.
148: You can:
149: Add more agents
150: Purchase add-ons
151: Upgrade or downgrade plans
152: Change billing cycles
153: View invoices
154: View subscription details
155: Log in as an Account Admin.
156: Go to Admin > Plans and Billing.
157: From this page, you can:
158: View your current plan details
159: Check billing frequency (monthly or annual)
160: Review active add-ons and agent count
161: Manage invoices and payment history
162: Auto-recharge subscription.
163: Add or remove agent seats
164: Your subscription cost is determined by the number of active agent seats in your plan.
165: Note: New agents can be added only if the payment mode is online. If you are paying offline, contact billing@freshworks.com.
166: When you add or remove agents:
167: Charges will be calculated pro rata for the remaining days in your billing cycle.
168: New agents are activated immediately once added.
169: When reducing the number of agents, ensure you delete the extra agents from your account first. The updated cost applies only after the extra agents are removed.
170: To add agent seats:
171: Go to Admin > Plans and Billing.
172: Click Manage Subscriptions.
173: Enter the number of additional agents you want to add.
174: Review the updated total price and click Update plan.
175: You can now invite and add more team members to your account. For details, see Add or Edit Support Agents.
176: To remove agent seats:
177: Before reducing seats, ensure you have removed extra agents from the agent configuration page so that you don’t exceed your available seats.
178: Go to Admin > Plans and Billing.
179: Click Manage Subscriptions and adjust the number of active agent seats.
180: Click Update plan.
181: View invoices
182: Your invoice will be automatically sent to your registered email address based on your billing cycle. Alternatively, you can view the invoice directly from the Plans & Billing page.
183: Note: This feature is available only for online payments that have a registered card on the portal. For accounts with offline modes of payment (bank transfers and PayPal), contact support@freshdesk.com.
184: To view your invoice:
185: Go to Admin > Plans and Billing.
186: In your current subscription plan card, click View Invoices.
187: You can view and download the invoices.
188: To change your email address, add the new email address in the right pane and click Update. You can add only one email address here.
189: Change billing cycle
190: You can choose to subscribe to paid plans on a monthly, quarterly, half-yearly, or annual basis. The billing date is automatically calculated from the subscription date. To change the date, contact billing@freshworks.com.
191: Go to Admin > Plans and Billing.
192: Click Manage Subscriptions.
193: Select the billing cycle from the top-right corner.
194: Click Update plan.
195: Purchase Freddy add-ons
196: Add-ons help you extend the functionality of your plan without changing your core plan tier. Freshdesk offers the following add-ons:
197: Freddy AI Agent
198: Freddy AI Copilot
199: For more details, see Manage Freddy AI Ad-ons.
200: Upgrade or downgrade plans
201: Easily switch to a higher or lower plan at any time, based on your business needs.
202: You can:
203: Upgrade to a higher plan: The upgrade will be applied immediately, and you’ll be charged a pro-rata amount for the remaining period in your current billing cycle.
204: Move to a lower plan: The change takes effect after your current billing cycle ends.
205: While switching plans, you can also update your agent count and add-ons (for example, Freddy AI Agent packs or Freddy Copilot agent licenses). When reducing the number of agents or removing add-ons, ensure you delete the extra agents from your account first.
206: For example, if you reduce your agent seats from 5 to 2, remove two agents from your account. The lower subscription cost applies only after the extra agents are removed.
207: Go to Admin > Plans and Billing.
208: Click Manage Subscriptions.
209: Switch to a higher or lower plan to upgrade or downgrade.

67: Model Context Protocol (MCP) integration in Freshdesk
68: Modified on: Mon, 5 Oct, 2026 at 11:37 AM
69: Applies to: Freshdesk, Freshdesk Omni 2026.
70: The Freshworks Model Context Protocol (MCP) server enables AI tools like Cursor and Claude to securely connect and interact with Freshdesk. The MCP server acts as middleware to expose specific capabilities, such as creating tickets, by using public APIs and supported authentication methods.
71: This article provides details about supported MCP integrations and how to configure them in your AI tools.
72: Note: Currently, Freshdesk allows you to authenticate requests involved in MCP integration by using an API key only.
73: TABLE OF CONTENTS
74: Supported plans and limits
75: Supported MCP integrations
76: Option 1: Set up MCP integration with Claude Code
77: Option 2: Set up MCP integration with Claude Desktop
78: Option 3: Set up MCP integration with Cursor
79: Option 4: Set up MCP integration with Microsoft Copilot Studio
80: Option 5: Set up MCP integration with Visual Studio Code
81: Troubleshoot issues
82: List of available tools
83: Pagination in MCP
84: Example prompts
85: Frequently Asked Questions (FAQs)
86: Freshworks MCP security
87: More resources
88: Supported plans and limits
89: This feature applies to the following products:
90: • Freshdesk Standalone 2021 (Latest version)
91: • Freshdesk Unified Omni 2026
92: Starting September 10, 2026, the Freshworks MCP integration is generally available. The rate limits and monthly action allowances for each plan are outlined below.
93: What counts as an MCP action?
94: An action is defined as a successful tool invocation via MCP. Examples of tool invocations. Examples:
95: • Fetch conversation related to the ticket with ID 1001 (1 action)
96: • Update the company name for the record with ID 11 to Apple (1 action)
97: Supported plans
98: Rate limits (actions per minute)
99: Included MCP actions (per account, annually)
100: Growth
101: 25
102: 1,200
103: Pro
104: 50
105: 6,000
106: Enterprise
107: 100
108: 12,000
109: Important:
110: • Pricing: To view current pricing and purchase add-on action packs, see Pricing.
111: • EAP transition:
112: • If you were on the Early Access Program (EAP), standard pricing and limits take effect on October 5, 2026.
113: • During the EAP, if you used the MCP integration on any plan other than Freshdesk Standalone 2021 (the latest version) or Freshdesk Unified Omni 2026 variant, the integration will stop working after September 10, 2026.
114: Supported MCP integrations
115: Freshdesk supports MCP integration with any AI tool that provides MCP support. This section highlights a selection of commonly used integrations that you can connect to Freshdesk.
116: Claude Code
117: Claude Desktop
118: Cursor
119: Microsoft Copilot Studio
120: Visual Studio Code
121: Option 1: Set up MCP integration with Claude Code
122: Connect and verify the MCP server within the Claude Code editor. After the setup is complete, Claude Code can use tools exposed by the MCP server directly within the editor.
123: Prerequisites
124: Before you begin, ensure you have the following:
125: The Claude Code app installed.
126: An active Claude account.
127: The Freshdesk MCP URL.
128: Note: Currently, custom domains are not supported for MCP endpoints. Ensure to use your Freshdesk base domain in the following format: https://<subdomain>.freshdesk.com/mcp
129: Create an MCP connection
130: To connect Claude Code to your MCP server, you must register the server using the http transport.
131: Run the following command in your terminal to register the Freshdesk MCP server:
132: claude mcp add my-remote-server --transport http https://<subdomain>.freshdesk.com/mcp --header "Authorization: <api-key>"
133: Expected output:
134: Added HTTP MCP server my-remote-server with URL: https://<subdomain>.freshdesk.com/mcp to local config
135: Headers: {
136: "Authorization": "<api-key>"
137: }
138: File modified: /Users/<username>/.claude.json [project: /Users/pmm]
139: Verify the connection
140: Use the following get command to confirm the server is listed as connected within the application:
141: claude mcp get my-remote-server
142: Expected output:
143: my-remote-server:
144: Scope: Local config (private to you in this project)
145: Status: ✓ Connected
146: Type: http
147: URL: https://<subdomain>.freshdesk.com/mcp
148: Headers:
149: Authorization: <api-key>
150: Option 2: Set up MCP integration with Claude Desktop
151: Connect and verify the MCP server within the Claude Desktop editor. After the setup is complete, Claude Desktop can use tools exposed by the MCP server directly within the editor.
152: Prerequisites
153: Before you begin, ensure you have the following:
154: The Claude Desktop app installed.
155: An active Claude account.
156: The Freshdesk MCP URL.
157: Note: Currently, custom domains are not supported for MCP endpoints. Ensure to use your Freshdesk base domain in the following format: https://<subdomain>.freshdesk.com/mcp
158: Create an MCP connection
159: To connect Claude Desktop to your MCP server, follow these steps:
160: Open Claude Desktop and go to Claude > Settings > Developer.
161: Select Edit Config. The claude_desktop_config.json file opens in your system's default text editor.
162: Copy and paste the following JSON configuration into the file. If other servers are already listed, add this as a new entry in the mcpServers object.
163: Note: Replace <mcp-url> with your specific server URL (for example, https://<subdomain>.freshdesk.com/mcp).
164: "mcpServers": {
165: "freshdesk-mcp": {
166: "command": "npx",
167: "args": [
168: "-y",
169: "mcp-remote",
170: "https://<subdomain>.freshdesk.com/mcp",
171: "--header",
172: "Authorization:<API_KEY>"
173: ]
174: }
175: }
176: Save the file and close the text editor.
177: Exit Claude Desktop by right-clicking the icon in the taskbar (Windows) or menu bar (macOS) and selecting Quit.
178: Relaunch Claude Desktop.
179: Follow the authentication prompts in your browser. After successful authentication, you can verify the connection status under Claude > Settings > Developer.
180: Option 3: Set up MCP integration with Cursor
181: Connect and verify the MCP server within the Cursor editor. After the setup is complete, Cursor can use tools exposed by the MCP server directly within the editor.
182: Prerequisites
183: Before you begin, ensure you have the following:
184: The Cursor app installed.
185: An active Cursor account.
186: The Freshdesk MCP URL.
187: Note: Currently, custom domains are not supported for MCP endpoints. Ensure to use your Freshdesk base domain in the following format: https://<subdomain>.freshdesk.com/mcp
188: Create an MCP connection
189: To connect Cursor to the MCP server, add the server details to your application's configuration file. To do so, follow these steps:
190: Open Cursor and go to the root folder of your project or user home directory for global configuration.
191: Create or update the .cursor/mcp.json file.
192: Add the following JSON object to the file:
193: Sample configuration using API key
194: {
195: "mcpServers": {
196: "freshdesk": {
197: "type": "http",
198: "url": "https://<subdomain>.freshdesk.com/mcp",
199: "headers": {
200: "Authorization": "<API-KEY>"
201: }
202: }
203: }
204: }
205: The following table describes the attributes used to configure the MCP server:
206: Attribute name
207: Description
208: mcpServers
209: List of all MCP servers to which the Cursor should connect.
210: Attribute of the mcpServers object
211: <name_of_the_MCP_object>
212: The unique name for your MCP server object.
213: Attribute of the <name_of_the_MCP_object> object
214: type
215: The protocol used by the MCP client to communicate with the MCP server.
216: url
217: The endpoint used by the MCP client to connect to your MCP server.
218: headers
219: Custom HTTP headers that the MCP client must send when connecting to your MCP server.
220: Note: Freshdesk supports authorization via API key only. In your configuration, include the "Authorization": "<YOUR_API_KEY>" attribute and replace <YOUR_API_KEY> with your actual Freshdesk API key.
221: Verify the configuration
222: After you save the configuration file, follow these steps to verify that Cursor can access the server and its tools:
223: In Cursor, go to View > Command Palette
224: Enter View: Open MCP Settings and select it from the list.
225: On the Tools page, locate the Installed MCP Servers section and verify your server name appears.
226: To view the available tools, expand the server card.
227: Once the connection is established, Cursor automatically retrieves the tools. You can invoke them through natural language prompts or allow Cursor to suggest them based on your current task.
228: If the server is offline or the configuration is incorrect, Cursor displays an error message provided by the MCP server in the settings view.
229: Option 4: Set up MCP integration with Microsoft Copilot Studio
230: Connect and verify the MCP server within the Microsoft Copilot Studio editor. After the setup is complete, Microsoft Copilot Studio can use tools exposed by the MCP server directly within the editor.
231: Prerequisites
232: Before you begin, ensure you have the following:
233: The Microsoft Copilot Studio app installed.
234: An active Microsoft Copilot Studio account.
235: An existing agent created within Microsoft Copilot Studio.
236: The Freshdesk MCP URL.
237: Note: Currently, custom domains are not supported for MCP endpoints. Ensure to use your Freshdesk base domain in the following format: https://<subdomain>.freshdesk.com/mcp
238: Create an MCP connection
239: To link Copilot Studio to your MCP server, follow these steps:
240: In the Copilot Studio dashboard, select Agents from the left navigation pane.
241: Select your agent from the list.
242: Open the Tools page for the agent.
243: Click + Add a tool at the top left of the page.
244: The Add tool window appears.
245: Select + New tool > Model Context Protocol.
246: The Add a Model Context Protocol server window appears.
247: Enter the following details:
248: Server name: Enter a name for the server.
249: Server description: Provide a short description of why the server is required.
250: Server URL: Enter the endpoint where the MCP client can reach your MCP server. For example, https://<subdomain>.freshdesk.com/mcp.
251: Authentication: Select the authentication mode as API key
252: Click Create.
253: After successful creation, the Add tool window appears to configure the connection.
254: In the Connection dropdown, you will see No connections available.
255: Click the dropdown and select Create new connection > Create.
256: In the authorization window, select your account name and click Continue.
257: After authorization succeeds, click Add and configure on the Add tool window.
258: You are redirected to the page for the newly created tool. Under the Tools section, you can view the list of available tools.
259: Verify the MCP connection
260: To confirm that your agent is actively connected to the Freshworks MCP server, follow these steps:
261: Go to your agent in Copilot Studio by selecting Agents and choosing the agent you want to verify.
262: The agent overview page opens.
263: Select Settings to open the agent settings page.
264: In the left navigation pane, select Connection Settings.
265: A table displays all connections associated with your agent.
266: For the newly configured connection, if the status is Not connected, click Connect.
267: The Create or pick a connection window appears.
268: Select the newly created connection and click Submit.
269: The status updates to Connected once the link is successfully established.
270: Option 5: Set up MCP integration with Visual Studio Code
271: Connect and verify the MCP server within the Visual Studio Code editor . After the setup is complete, Visual Studio Code can use tools exposed by the MCP server directly within the editor.
272: Prerequisites
273: Before you begin, ensure you have the following:
274: The Visual Studio Code app installed.
275: The MCP extension for VS Code installed.
276: The Freshdesk MCP URL.
277: Note: Currently, custom domains are not supported for MCP endpoints. Ensure to use your Freshdesk base domain in the following format: https://<subdomain>.freshdesk.com/mcp
278: Create an MCP connection
279: To integrate the MCP server into your VS Code environment, follow these steps:
280: Launch VS Code.
281: Open the Command Palette by pressing Ctrl+Shift+P (Windows) or Cmd+Shift+P (macOS).
282: Enter and select MCP: Open User Configuration.
283: Add the following JSON object to the mcp.json file and save it.
284: {
285: "servers": {
286: "my-remote-server": {
287: "type": "http",
288: "url": "https://<subdomain>.freshdesk.com/mcp",
289: "headers": {
290: "Authorization": "<api-key>"
291: }
292: }
293: }
294: }
295: A Start button appears above the my-remote-server entry. Click Start to initialize the server.
296: The following output appears to confirm the server is active:
297: Verify the configuration
298: After setting up your connection, you can confirm the server is running using either of the following methods:
299: View active servers: Open the Command Palette and select MCP: List Servers. Ensure your Freshdesk server is listed as active.
300: Review raw config: Open your mcp.json file to verify the server details and configuration target.
301: You can now run MCP-specific commands directly within your VS Code terminal or command palette to interact with Freshdesk data.
302: Troubleshoot issues
303: Issue: Connection failures
304: If the connection verification fails, check the following:
305: Network: Check your active internet connection and VPN status.
306: URL Accessibility: Open https://<subdomain>.freshdesk.com/mcp in your browser to ensure the endpoint is live.
307: Authentication: Verify that a valid API key is included in the authorization header.
308: Issue: MCP connection fails due to IP restrictions
309: Symptoms
310: MCP server connection fails despite correct endpoint configuration
311: Timeout or connection refused errors when running mcp-remote
312: Connection works in some networks but fails in restricted environments
313: Possible cause
314: Your Freshdesk or your organization’s network, enforces IP restrictions that block requests to or from the MCP server. If the required IP ranges are not allowlisted, the connection cannot be established.
315: Resolution
316: Allowlist required IP ranges:
317: Add the following IP ranges to your allowlist based on your data center/region:

319: AU: 10.3.0.0/16

321: EUC: 10.113.0.0/16
322: USE: 10.111.0.0/16, 10.113.0.0/16
323: EUN: 10.96.80.0/20

326: 10.17.144.0/20
327: 10.25.128.0/18
328: EUC:
329: 10.17.104.0/21
330: 10.25.192.0/18
331: IN:
332: 10.17.128.0/20
333: AU:
334: 10.17.96.0/21
335: EUN:
336: 10.97.216.0/21
337: Update IP restriction settings:
338: Configure IP restrictions in your Freshworks account.
339: Verify network access:
340: Ensure outbound HTTPS (port 443) is allowed
341: Confirm no firewall or proxy is blocking these IP ranges
342: Retry the connection:
343: Run: npx -y mcp-remote https://<subdomain>.freshdesk.com/mcp
344: Verification
345: MCP connection succeeds without timeout or network errors
346: MCP client shows the server status as Connected
347: Next steps

349: Verify region alignment between your Freshdesk account and configured IP ranges

467: Pagination in MCP
468: When an MCP tool returns many results, such as a list of solution articles, sending the entire payload at once can exceed token limits or cause the LLM to truncate the data. Large payloads can also slow down response times and reduce the accuracy of the AI.
469: To prevent this, the MCP server uses pagination to deliver results in smaller, manageable batches. This ensures the LLM processes information efficiently while staying within its operational limits.
470: The pagination process provides the following benefits:
471: Automatic processing: The MCP client and the LLM handle subsequent data requests automatically using the nextCursor parameter.
472: No manual configuration: You don't need to manage page numbers, cursors, or page sizes manually.
473: Optimized performance: Smaller response batches ensure more reliable processing and faster response times from the AI tool.

162: Frequently Asked Questions
163: How does the 14-day free trial work?
164: When you sign up, you instantly get access to our Enterprise plan for 14 days. We will alert you before your trial expires. You can then select a plan and pay by credit card to continue using the product. If you choose not to continue, your account will be suspended.
165: Can I upgrade or downgrade my subscription?
166: Yes, you can choose to upgrade your subscription instantly. If you wish to downgrade or cancel your subscription, you can do so at the end of your term. Click on ‘Billing’ in your Freshdesk account to modify your subscription details.
167: Do you have any cancellation fees?
168: No. Freshdesk is a pay-as-you-go service. We do not have any cancellation fees. You can cancel whenever you want, but your cancellation will come into effect only after the end of your term.
169: What types of payment do you accept?
170: We accept Visa, Mastercard, Discover, and American Express. We do not accept PayPal. We will not be able to accept purchase orders over the phone. All of our offline payments follow USD pricing.
171: What is a session in Freddy AI Agent?
172: A session is a unique interaction between an end-user and an AI Agent.
173: In Freddy AI Agent Studio, an Email AI Agent session is defined as a 72-hour window starting from the customer’s first email. All AI responses within that window count as a single session, regardless of the number of replies.
174: How can I buy additional Freddy AI Agent sessions?
175: You can purchase any number of AI agent session packs. The validity corresponds to your payment cycle. For example, if you choose to pay quarterly, your sessions will also expire quarterly.
176: Do I need to purchase Freddy AI Copilot for all agents?
177: No, Freddy AI Copilot can be purchased and assigned to any number of agents of your choice.
178: Do I get free Freddy AI Agent sessions on any plan?
179: We offer 500 free sessions on the Growth, Pro, and Enterprise plans to try out Freddy AI Agent. This is limited to once per account. Once exhausted, you need to buy additional sessions based on your needs.
180: Are day passes available for Freddy AI Copilot?
181: No, day passes are not available for Freddy AI Copilot.
182: What are connector app tasks?
183: We offer pre-built connectors to make data sync and workflow automation with any external application simple. Here’s a list of connector apps that we offer. You will consume tasks when any of these connector apps are used.

377: Introduction
378: Here is Front's Core API, a backend API that gives comprehensive control over all entities in Front from Contacts to Comments.
379: Guides
380: Refer to the following guides to learn how to use the Core API:
381: Getting Started
382: Fundamentals
383: Tools
384: Sample Application
385: API Terminology 101
386: Authentication
387: Front supports OAuth2.0 as well as API Tokens. To learn about authenticating with Front, see our guide on authentication.
388: Base URL
389: API calls will always work with https://api2.frontapp.com as the base URL. However, the API may return resource URLs that include your company's name, such as https://acme.api.frontapp.com. If the API is returning URLs like those, you can call it either with api2.frontapp.com or acme.api.frontapp.com.
390: Rate Limits
391: To ensure an acceptable response time from our API and facilitate access for all customers, Front implements an overall rate limit as well as several "burst" limits for certain endpoints. For more on these limits, please see here.
392: Content Type
393: The API is designed to communicate with your server using JSON. All responses coming from the API will send data in a valid JSON object. If you need to send data to the API, your request should set the Content-Type HTTP header to application/json.
394: Some endpoints also support multipart requests for file upload. For more details about it, please check our multipart request documentation.
395: Search parameters
396: For some requests to get a large collection of resources, you can send search criteria in the query string via a parameter named q.
397: Parameters for Conversations
398: Parameters for Events
399: Parameters for Contacts
400: File Upload
401: When you want to send files through the API, your request needs to be sent using the Content-Type HTTP header set to multipart/form-data.
402: The JSON data you would normally send in the request body needs to be split in multiple form fields (one for each property) named after the property key. If the property is an array, the name should include the index of the data (ie: {"to": [[email protected], [email protected]]} would be split in two fields named to[0], to[1]).
403: 📘
404: Restriction on files (type and size) depends on the endpoint. If your request doesn't comply to those limitations, the response will contain an error describing the issue.
405: Dates
406: All dates in the Front API are encoded as a number representing Unix time: It is the number of seconds that have elapsed since 00:00:00 UTC, January 1st 1970.
407: Since Front is based on events that can occur during the same second, all the timestamps include leap seconds with a precision of 3 digits: 1454453901.012.
408: Deprecation Policy
409: Read our deprecation policy to learn how Front communicates about changes that may affect your integrations.

99: OAuth
100: Intro to Front OAuth
101: OAuth 2.0 is a protocol that lets external applications request authorization to API access in a secure way. When you set up OAuth in your app, you specify which scopes the OAuth token will have access to. Customers installing your app are then asked to authorize the requested scopes so that data is sent to you from their customer instance.
102: Each OAuth application is assigned a unique Client ID and Client Secret which will be used in the authorization flow. The Client Secret should never be shared. To obtain your OAuth credentials, refer to Create, manage, and publish apps.
103: 📘
104: OAuth is required for public integrations available to all Front customers unless you obtain an exception from us. OAuth makes it much easier for customers to install your integration through our App Store.
105: 📘
106: End users authorizing OAuth apps must be admins. This applies to both private and public OAuth apps.
107: The only exception is when authorizing OAuth for our MCP server. That connection uses user-scoped tokens, so any Front teammate can authorize it.
108: At a glance
109: These are the main URLs that our OAuth process utilizes.
110: URLValue
111: Authorizationhttps://app.frontapp.com/oauth/authorize
112: Token & refresh URLhttps://app.frontapp.com/oauth/token
113: Token scopes
114: Refer to the Authentication topic to learn about the scopes available to your OAuth token.
115: Using OAuth with Front
116: Front's OAuth implementation only supports the authorization code grant type which defines a flow to get a temporary authorization token which can then be exchanged to get an API and refresh token.
117: 1. Request authorization
118: To request Front API access, you need to redirect the user to https://app.frontapp.com/oauth/authorize?response_type=code&client_id=<CLIENTID>&redirect_uri=<REDIRECTURI>.
119: cURL
120: GET https://app.frontapp.com/oauth/authorize?response_type=code&client_id={clientId}&redirect_uri={redirectURI} HTTP/1.1
121: Host: app.frontapp.com
122: // You should replace "{clientID}" and "{redirectURI}" by the values of your OAuth application.
123: NameTypeDescription
124: response_typestringMust be set to code.
125: client_idstringClient ID of your OAuth application.
126: redirect_uristringThe URL in your application where users will be redirected after authorization.
127: statestring (optional)Used to protect against cross-site request forgery attacks.
128: 2. Get an authorization code
129: If the user accepts the authorization request, Front will redirect them back to the redirect URL specified in the first step. The request will contain a code parameter as well as the state you provided in the first step. Extract the value of code from the URL to use it in the next step.
130: If the states don't match, you should consider the request as insecure and the process should be aborted.
131: cURL
132: GET https://yoursite.example.com/example_path?code={authorizationCode}&state={state} HTTP/1.1
133: Host: yoursite.example.com
134: // The HTTP request will depend on the param redirect_uri specified in the authorization request.
135: NameTypeDescription
136: codestringTemporary authorization code to exchange for an API token.
137: statestring (optional)State provided in the authorization request.
138: 3. Exchange authorization code
139: Once your application receives the temporary authorization code, you need to exchanged it for an API token by sending a POST HTTP request to https://app.frontapp.com/oauth/token with the body parameters noted in the table below.
140: Your request MUST be authenticated with Basic authentication using your OAuth application Client ID and Client Secret base64 encoded, as shown below:
141: 📘
142: Use Basic Authentication to request a token, then Bearer Authentication after that
143: Basic authentication is only used when making OAuth requests to the https://app.frontapp.com/ OAuth service. Otherwise, authentication will be Bearer authentication as stated in the rest of these docs.
144: 📘
145: 💡 Basic Authentication
146: The Basic Authentication string is your client ID and secret joined with a colon (:), then Base64 encoded.
147: For example, if:
148: client_id = 123abcclient_secret = 456def
149: The string before Base64 encoding is:
150: 123abc:456def
151: The string after Base64 encoding is:
152: MTIzYWJjOjQ1NmRlZg==
153: The final header to send in the request is:
154: Authorization: Basic MTIzYWJjOjQ1NmRlZg==
155: Front's OAuth server response will include two tokens (the API token in the access_token param and the refresh token in the refresh_token param) and the access_token expiration time in the expires_at param.
156: Please store the refresh_token securely, as it is required to obtain a new access_token in the next step.
157: cURLResponse
158: POST https://app.frontapp.com/oauth/token HTTP/1.1
159: Host: app.frontapp.com
160: Authorization: Basic <your_basic_credentials>
161: Response 200
162: {
163: "access_token" : "",
164: "refresh_token": "",
165: "expires_at" : "",
166: "token_type" : "Bearer"
167: }
168: Body parameterTypeDescription
169: codestringThe temporary authorization code received in step 2.
170: redirect_uristringThe URL in your application where users will be redirected after authorization.
171: It MUST be the same URL as the one used in the step to request an authorization code.
172: grant_typestringThe grant type used to get the authorization code. Needs to be authorization_code
173: 👍
174: When implementing OAuth for application channels, you can leverage token instrospection URLs
175: After obtaining an access token for an application channel, you can allow the external service to provide a custom channel name and address during the OAuth flow by using the token instrospection for channel identification.
176: 4. Use Refresh Token to obtain new tokens
177: When the access_token from Step 3 has expired after an hour, it will need be be refreshed to continue usage. When requesting resources with an expired access_token, Front's OAuth server response will return a 401 error status code, denoting that the access_token has expired.
178: To obtain a new access_token, send a POST request to https://app.frontapp.com/oauth/token with the refresh_token acquired in Step 3 and grant_type set to refresh_token. Refresh tokens are valid for 6 months, so as long as you request a new access token within that period, you will not have to restart the OAuth process from Step 1. Similar to Step 3, your request MUST be authenticated with Basic authentication using your OAuth application Client ID and Client Secret.
179: 📘
180: Refresh tokens expire after 6 months, but aren't refreshed until the last 24 hours of expiry
181: When you first receive a refresh token, it will have an expiration date set six months out. You should note this expiration date. During the six months of validity, the API will return the same refresh token to you when you obtain new tokens. In the last 24 hours of validity, however, the API will return a new refresh token, which will then start a new six month period of validity. Therefore, it is important to request new tokens in the last 24 hours of the refresh token's validity period to continue extending this timeframe without having to restart the entire OAuth process.
182: The Front OAuth server response will include two new tokens, the access_token and the refresh_token. Store this new set of values for further use. The access token expires in 60 minutes, and the refresh token in 6 months.
183: Repeat this process as necessary, making sure to use the refresh token at least once before its 6 month expiration so that you can get a new set of credentials without restarting the OAuth process from Step 1.
184: cURLResponse
185: POST https://app.frontapp.com/oauth/token HTTP/1.1
186: Host: app.frontapp.com
187: Authorization: Basic <your_basic_credentials>
188: Response 200
189: {
190: "access_token" : "",
191: "refresh_token": "",
192: "expires_at" : "",
193: "token_type" : "Bearer"
194: }
195: Body parameterTypeDescription
196: refresh_tokenstringThe refresh token received in step 3.
197: grant_typestringThe grant type used to get the authorization code. Needs to be refresh_token

326: Frequently asked questions
327: What are your Success Services packages and how much do they cost?
328: Front offers 3 Success Services packages: Professional Onboarding, Enterprise Onboarding, and Success Services project hours. You can view pricing and what's included in each package here. To ensure you're set up for success, we require an onboarding package be purchased for contracts over $25k.
329: How does Front’s free trial work? Do I need a credit card?
330: Our free 14-day trial offers all the features available in our Professional plan. You can get started without a credit card and can upgrade at any time during your trial. You do not need a credit card to start, continue, or complete your Front trial.
331: What is a seat?
332: A seat is a paid Front license that can be granted to a unique user in your organization.
333: What is a channel?
334: A channel is the communication medium that people use to get in touch with you like email, SMS, chat (Resolve), WhatsApp, and more.
335: Can I connect multiple channel types with the Starter plan?
336: No, the Starter plan only supports a single channel type of Email, chat (Resolve), or SMS. The Professional and Enterprise plan support multiple channel types.
337: What is the maximum number of channels per plan?
338: Your channel maximum depends on both your plan and number of licenses. On Starter, you can connect up to 10 channels per license, with Professional up to 30 per license, and with Enterprise up to 50 per license. For example, a team of 5 users on Professional would have a maximum of 150 channels. Please see our help article for more details.
339: Which providers power Front AI features?
340: We’re using OpenAI, Azure OpenAI, and Amazon AWS, which are industry-leading AI providers. Specifically, we use the text generation API.
341: How is my data processed? Is my data protected?
342: While we may use your data to further train your model, your data will never be cross-contaminated with other companies’ data. We also have extensive agreements in place with our AI providers to ensure that they’re not training their foundational models on any data that we send to them.
343: How can I learn more about Front’s security and compliance best practices?
344: Ensuring your data’s confidentiality, integrity, and availability is core to our mission and platform. Read more here about Front’s security, privacy and compliance practices. You also may request access to our security documentation by reaching out to your sales representative.
345: Can I combine seats across multiple plans?
346: No, plans are assigned at the organization level. You can add or remove seats as needed within a single plan.
347: Can I pay with my bank instead of my credit card?
348: You can pay by wire transfer or ACH if you purchase annually and the total contract value is over $12K. Reach out to [email protected] to have your payment method updated.

231: ## Querying This Documentation
232: This site has an agentic ask interface you may use to query the documentation dynamically by asking a question.
233: Perform an HTTP GET request on the following URL with the `ask` and `goal` query parameters:
234: ```
235: GET https://docs.usepylon.com/pylon-docs/index.md?ask=<question>&goal=<user_goal>
236: ```
237: `ask` is the immediate question: it should be specific, self-contained, and written in natural language.
238: `goal` is what the user is ultimately trying to achieve, the reason they need the answer. Sharing it helps GitBook give you a better, more relevant answer. A goal is most helpful when it describes the outcome the user wants rather than restating the question. For example, with `ask=how do I create an API token`, a goal like `automate deployments from our CI pipeline` lets GitBook tailor the answer to that use case.
239: The response will contain a direct answer to the question and relevant excerpts and sources from the documentation.

1265: Frequently asked questions
1266: How is Pylon priced?
1267: Pylon is priced based on the number of seats and the number of agentic credits your team needs. Because B2B support teams vary significantly in size and workflow, pricing reflects your team's unique needs. Book a demo and we'll put together a quote specific to your setup.
1268: Is pricing per seat, per ticket, or per account?
1269: Pylon's pricing is seat-based and credit usage-based. You're not charged per ticket, so your costs stay predictable as your customer base grows, even as ticket volume scales.
1270: What's included in every plan?
1271: Every plan includes core ticketing, unified ticketing (Slack, email, and chat widget), omnichannel support, a knowledge base, NPS and CSAT surveys, and analytics.
1272: Are AI features included, or are they a separate add-on?
1273: Pylon's agentic features (including the Assist Agent, Automations, Support Agent, and Slack Agent) are accessible when you purchase credits, not sold as separate add-ons.
1274: Does Pylon offer annual and monthly billing, and is there a discount for paying annually?
1275: Pylon offers both annual and monthly billing. When you commit to credits upfront, you will receive a discount.
1276: Do I have to buy credits upfront?
1277: No. Pylon offers both pay-as-you-go credits and committed credit plans, so teams can buy credits as they need them or commit upfront. You can purchase additional credits in-product anytime.
1278: Is there a minimum seat requirement or minimum contract size?
1279: There is a minimum seat count for new customers. Pylon is built for B2B support teams rather than solo operators, so it's designed to deliver value at team scale.
1280: What does a contract with Pylon look like?
1281: Standard contracts are annual. Multi-year agreements are available for teams that want rate lock and additional flexibility. Credits can be used across the entire contract term and buying more at once will result in a higher credit discount.
1282: What counts as a "seat"?
1283: A seat covers any teammate who needs to work tickets, including agents and admins with inbox access. Stakeholders who only need visibility into conversations, without working them, can use a viewer seat.
1284: Do you have viewer seats?

692: AI agents
693: An AI agent is an AI worker with its own instructions, AI model and permissions. It can chat with visitors, reply to tickets and sort them.
694: Your plan sets how many AI agents you can create: Starter 1, Team 5, Business 50, Enterprise unlimited.
695: One AI agent can work in many places, for example the same chatbot on three websites. It still counts once.
696: What AI agents do in LiveAgent
697: Built in, no AI agent needed
698: These run on your AI provider too, but they don't use an AI agent, so they don't count toward your LiveAgent plan.
699: Summaries
700: Call transcripts
701: Translations
702: Frequently asked questions
703: Black Friday
704: How do I get the Black Friday price?
705: Choose a plan and pay by December 15, 2026 with the code for your billing: BLACKFRIDAY40Y takes 40% off annual billing for the first year, BLACKFRIDAY33M takes 33% off monthly billing for the first 12 bills. After that, your plan's regular price applies. It works on every plan, Enterprise included, for new and existing customers. The discount applies to the plan and billing period you pay for with the code.
706: Plans and billing
707: Is there a free trial?
708: Yes. Every plan starts with a 30-day free trial, and no credit card is required. When the trial ends, upgrade to a paid plan to keep your account and everything you set up.
709: Can I change or cancel my plan at any time?
710: Yes. You can upgrade or downgrade at any time, except in the 24 hours before your billing day. If you cancel, your account stays active until the end of the period you paid for.
711: Can my price go up?
712: No. Your plan keeps its regular price for as long as you keep the plan, also when you add agents. A discount you get with a code ends when its period is over. We may change the prices of our plans, but a new price applies only to new customers and to customers who change plan. Moving up within 12 months? Ask us for a special quote.
713: Is there a contract or a setup fee?
714: No setup fees and no long-term commitment: pay monthly and cancel anytime, or pay annually and pay less per agent. Buying through procurement? With an annual plan we provide a written quote and a contract: request a quote.
715: How does LiveAgent's price compare with Zendesk?
716: Our Zendesk pricing guide puts Zendesk's current plans and add-ons next to LiveAgent's. Moving over is free: see Zendesk migration.
717: Can you help me migrate from another help desk?
718: Yes, free on every paid plan: our built-in importers move tickets, contacts and the knowledge base from Zendesk, Freshdesk, Help Scout and other help desks. Large accounts can take several hours or even days to import. How migration works.
719: Which payment methods do you accept?
720: All major credit cards (Visa, Mastercard, Maestro, American Express, Diners), Apple Pay, Google Pay, PayPal, and wire transfer on annual plans. Prices are in USD and exclude VAT. Customers in the EU are invoiced in EUR. VAT is added where it applies: an EU company with a valid VAT ID outside Slovakia pays no VAT (reverse charge) when it enters the VAT ID in its account.
721: What do phone calls cost?
722: LiveAgent charges nothing for calls. Your call center runs on your own phone provider, which bills you directly for phone numbers and minutes.
723: Do you offer a startup discount?
724: Early-stage startups can apply for a special startup deal.
725: How much do I save with annual billing?
726: Up to 21% per agent; how much depends on the plan. Switch between monthly and annual billing above the plans: each card shows your team's monthly total for that billing.
727: How is Enterprise priced?
728: A flat monthly fee that includes 80 agents, about $50 per agent (about $40 on annual billing). Extra agents are $49 / month, or $39 / month on annual billing.
729: What is the difference between Business and Enterprise?
730: Business is billed per agent, for any team size, with higher limits than Team. Enterprise is a flat fee with 80 agents included, the highest limits and a dedicated account manager.
731: AI features
732: How much does AI cost?
733: A typical AI chat costs about $0.11 at your AI provider, so 300 chats a month cost about $33–$81 (at our median and our average); LiveAgent adds nothing on top. $0.11 is the median in LiveAgent's own support in October 2026 (how we measured it, with the average and our newest chat flow). Drafting replies with AI Answer Assistant costs about $2–3 per 1,000 replies with a low-cost model such as Claude Haiku (our estimate from the providers' list prices, October 2026). The cost depends on the model you choose, the tools an AI agent uses and the length of the chat.
734: Do I need an AI provider account?
735: Yes. AI features run on your own OpenAI, Anthropic, Google Gemini or FlowHunt account, and you pay the provider directly, only for what you use. Your AI provider processes the text under your agreement with it.
736: Does LiveAgent charge for AI?
737: No. No AI fees, no token markup, no per-resolution fees: you pay only your AI provider, for what you use. For AI, plans differ only in the number of AI agents.
738: What if I need more AI agents than my plan includes?
739: You can move to a higher plan. Enterprise includes unlimited AI agents.
740: What is the MCP server on Business and Enterprise?
741: On every plan, your AI agents use LiveAgent's built-in tools. On Business and Enterprise, you can also connect external AI tools, such as Claude, to LiveAgent through its MCP server.
742: Are there any usage limits?
743: Each plan except Enterprise has a limit on the number of AI agents. Where a plan says "unlimited", there is no plan limit, but to keep LiveAgent fast and reliable for everyone, we apply technical and rate limits to AI agents, the API and the MCP server to prevent misuse.
744: Footer
745: LiveAgent is help desk and call center software for small and growing support teams, in business since 2004.
746: Email, live chat, phone, social media and WhatsApp in one shared inbox, with a knowledge base, AI that answers customers and drafts replies, and integrations like Shopify.

388: Can I add more Inboxes or Docs sites to my plan?
389: Yes — additional Inboxes beyond the number included in your plan are available for $10 per month when paid annually (or $12 per month). Additional Docs sites are available for $20 per month when paid annually (or $24 per month). The Free plan is limited to just 1 Inbox and 1 Docs site.
390: What counts as an AI resolution?
391: A resolution is a single conversation that is resolved by Envoy's built-in AI agent, Scout, without human assistance.
392: A resolution is counted only if the customer receives an AI response and doesn’t use escalation, search the knowledge base, ask more questions, or indicate that they need more help.
393: If a customer requests more help with natural language or by selecting the “I still need help” button, the conversation won’t count as a resolution and you won’t be charged.
394: You'll only be charged for one resolution per conversation, even if Scout responds to multiple questions.
395: Can I set caps on AI resolution spending?
396: Yes — you can set a monthly cap on Envoy resolutions. If you hit your spending cap, your AI agent will be disabled automatically for the remainder of the monthly cycle. You’ll receive email notifications as you get closer to your cap.
397: This option allows for predictable billing, so you’ll never be surprised at the end of the month.
398: How does the free trial work?
399: When you sign up for a free trial of the Standard or Plus plan, you’ll get 15 days to take all of the plan’s features for a test drive — no credit card required. Want to trial the Pro plan? Talk to our sales team.
400: How does the 3-month Envoy trial work?
401: When you create your Help Scout account, you will get 3 months of free, unlimited Envoy resolutions. This gives you plenty of time to test and measure the impact without having to pay for resolutions. The trial starts on the first day you create your account.
402: What payment methods does Help Scout accept?
403: We accept major credit cards, including Visa, American Express, Mastercard, and Discover. For some annual payments, wire or ACH transfer is also available. Free accounts don’t need to add a payment method.
404: Do you offer discounts for startups or non-profits?
405: The Help Scout for Good program offers discounts for qualifying non-profits and B Corporations. We also have a startup plan designed to accommodate early-stage companies. Check it out to see if you qualify.
406: Ready to go?
407: Learn the platform in less than an hour and become a power user in less than a day.

184: Introduction
185: 📘
186: Before you start
187: Please make sure to check out our Quickstart guide to make sure you understand the difference between Private and Public apps and to learn about the steps you need to follow when building them.
188: The Gorgias API is structured with REST in mind. Our API has predictable resource-oriented URLs, accepts JSON-encoded request bodies, returns JSON-encoded responses, and uses standard HTTP response codes, authentication, and verbs.
189: On this page, you'll find the complete REST API reference, examples, definitions of objects, and guides.
